title: Ransomware-style file encryption on a file server
description: Over one night the files on a departmental file server were renamed and became unreadable, and a note demanding payment appeared on the server. The investigation aimed to establish how the attacker gained access, what was affected, and whether backups were harmed. The case was closed after the final report was accepted.

sources.label: File server FS-02
sources.description: Departmental file server holding shared project folders.

sources.label: Backup appliance BK-01
sources.description: Appliance that stores nightly backups of file servers.

sources.label: Switch mirror port capture
sources.description: Copy of traffic to and from the file server.

evidence.title: Disk image of the FS-02 data volume
evidence.description: Forensic image of the encrypted data volume of the file server, taken after the server was shut down.
evidence.text: Volume 4 TB. 183,402 files renamed with the extension .locked between 01:12 and 03:48. Original file names preserved before the extension.
custody: Handed over for file system analysis

analyses.notes: File system and encryption pattern review.
findings: Files renamed in a fixed order across all folders
The encryption touched project folders alphabetically, starting with the oldest data. This fits a scripted tool, not manual action.
medium
Original contents unrecoverable from the volume
The files contain high-entropy data throughout, and no unencrypted copies were found on the volume.
high

evidence.title: File change log showing mass renaming
evidence.description: File server change log listing the rename operations during the incident.
evidence.text:
2026-05-09 01:12:03 rename path=//fs02/projects/alpha/plan.docx -> plan.docx.locked user=SYSTEM process=svc_update.exe
2026-05-09 01:12:03 rename path=//fs02/projects/alpha/budget.xlsx -> budget.xlsx.locked user=SYSTEM process=svc_update.exe
Summary: 183,402 renames, rate about 17 per second.

findings: All renames made by a single unfamiliar process
Every rename was performed by a program named svc_update.exe running as the system account, which is not part of the server's standard software.
high
Encryption ran for about two and a half hours
The renames started at 01:12 and stopped at 03:48 at a steady rate, which indicates the process ran unattended.
medium

evidence.title: Ransom note text file found on the server
evidence.description: Text file left in every folder of the file server, demanding payment.
evidence.text: All your files have been encrypted. To get them back, contact recover-files@mail-example.test within 72 hours and quote ID 7A21-F9. Do not rename the files or use recovery tools.

findings: Note names a contact address and a deadline
The note demands contact within 72 hours at an anonymous mailbox. No payment amount or wallet is included in the note itself.
info

evidence.title: Screenshot of the ransom note on the server console
evidence.description: Screenshot of the server console showing the note displayed at login.
evidence.notes: Photographed because the screen could not be captured digitally.

findings: Photo time is consistent with the shutdown log
The camera timestamp is about ten minutes before the recorded shutdown of the server.
info

evidence.title: Memory dump of FS-02 taken before shutdown
evidence.description: Capture of the server's memory taken just before it was powered off.
evidence.text: Process svc_update.exe (PID 3320) started 01:11:48 by a scheduled task. Parent service: Task Scheduler. Open handles on 214 files under the projects share.

findings: Encrypting process was started by a scheduled task
The program was started by the task scheduler one minute before the first rename, so a task must have been created beforehand by someone with administrator access.
high

evidence.title: Event log entries for shadow copy deletion
evidence.description: System event log entries around the start of the encryption.
evidence.text:
2026-05-09 01:10:22 ProcessCreate Image=C:/Windows/System32/vssadmin.exe CommandLine="vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet" User=SYSTEM
2026-05-09 01:10:25 ProcessCreate Image=C:/Windows/System32/wbadmin.exe CommandLine="wbadmin delete catalog -quiet" User=SYSTEM

findings: Local recovery points deleted before encryption
Commands that delete local snapshots and the backup catalogue ran about two minutes before the encryption began, which removes the easiest way to restore files.
high

evidence.title: SMB traffic capture during the encryption
evidence.description: Copy of the file-sharing traffic between the file server and the office network during the incident.
evidence.text:
01:09:55 192.0.2.201 -> 192.0.2.20:445 SMB2 session setup user=svc_backup status=success
01:10:01 192.0.2.201 -> 192.0.2.20:445 SMB2 tree connect //fs02/ADMIN$
Summary: 1 internal source address, 0 connections to outside addresses.

findings: Access came from one internal workstation using a service account
The administrative session originated from an internal address and used a backup service account, not a person's own account.
high
No outside connections seen from the server
The server made no connections to outside addresses during the capture, so there was no sign of data being sent out from the server.
info

evidence.title: Remote desktop logon events for FS-02
evidence.description: Remote desktop sign-in events on the server in the 48 hours before the encryption.
evidence.text:
2026-05-08 22:41:03 logon type=10 user=svc_backup source=192.0.2.201 result=success
2026-05-08 22:41:30 logon type=10 user=svc_backup source=192.0.2.201 result=success
2026-05-07 14:02:17 logon type=10 user=svc_backup source=192.0.2.201 result=failure count=26

findings: Many failed sign-ins followed by a success
Twenty-six failed remote desktop sign-ins for the backup service account came from one address the day before the successful sign-in. This pattern fits password guessing.
high
Remote desktop access used by a service account
Service accounts are normally not used for interactive sessions. The sessions at 22:41 were interactive.
medium

evidence.title: Backup job log showing deleted jobs
evidence.description: Log of the backup appliance showing job changes before the incident.
evidence.text:
2026-05-08 23:58:40 job_deleted name=FS02-nightly user=svc_backup source=192.0.2.201
2026-05-08 23:58:52 retention_changed name=FS02-weekly keep=0 user=svc_backup

findings: Backup jobs removed an hour before encryption
The nightly and weekly backup jobs for the file server were deleted or set to keep nothing about an hour before the encryption, which would have removed all restore points.
high
Offline backup copy was not affected
A monthly offline copy stored away from the appliance was unaffected and was later used to restore data.
info

evidence.title: Registry export showing disabled antivirus protection
evidence.description: Export of the server's antivirus configuration keys.
evidence.text:
HKLM/SOFTWARE/Policies/Microsoft/Windows Defender  DisableAntiSpyware=1
HKLM/SOFTWARE/Policies/Microsoft/Windows Defender/Real-Time Protection  DisableRealtimeMonitoring=1  LastWrite=2026-05-08 22:49:11

findings: Real-time protection switched off the night before
Antivirus real-time monitoring was disabled by policy about eight minutes after the first remote desktop sign-in, which explains why the encrypting program ran unhindered.
high

evidence.title: Recovery timeline from the infrastructure team
evidence.description: Timeline document written by the infrastructure team during the response.
evidence.text: 08:30 Server found unresponsive. 08:42 Network cable removed. 09:15 Memory captured. 09:40 Server powered off. Restore from the offline monthly copy completed on 2026-05-13.
evidence.notes: Written by the infrastructure team, not by the investigators.

evidence.title: Disk image of the workstation used for the remote sessions
evidence.description: Forensic image of the internal workstation from which the remote desktop sessions originated.
evidence.text: NTFS volume 953 GB. Scheduled task svc_update_job created 2026-05-08 23:12. Credential dumping tool found in a temporary folder, deleted 2026-05-09 04:02.
evidence.notes: Workstation belonged to a contractor and was already out of service.

findings: Credential theft tool recovered from deleted files
A tool that extracts stored passwords was recovered from deleted files on the workstation, which fits how the backup service account password could have been obtained.
high
Workstation was the origin of the remote sessions
The scheduled task that started the encrypting program was created from this workstation, which ties the earlier sessions to the encryption.
high

links: The remote desktop sessions by the backup account were followed by deletion of backup jobs within the hour.
Deleted backup jobs and deleted local snapshots both prepared the system for the encryption.
The shadow copy deletion commands ran about two minutes before the first rename in the change log.
The change log and the disk image show the same number of renamed files and the same extension.
The workstation image shows the origin of the sessions listed in the remote desktop log.
Disabled antivirus protection was changed shortly before the shadow copy commands ran.
